slot.brief: Given a disaccharide (e.g. maltose/lactose/sucrose), test multiple statements about glycosidic linkage type, reducing nature and hydrolysis products; pick the correct combination.

stem: For lactose, consider the statements: I. Its glycosidic linkage is $\beta(1\to4)$. II. It is a non-reducing disaccharide. III. On hydrolysis, it yields glucose and galactose. Which statements are correct?

verdicts.working: Lactose has a β(1→4) linkage and hydrolyses to glucose and galactose. Its free anomeric carbon makes it reducing, so II is false.

working:
Lactose has a $\beta(1\to4)$ linkage.
Its glucose residue has a free anomeric carbon, so lactose is reducing.
Hydrolysis gives glucose and galactose.
Correct: I and III.

Independent check: Lactose has a β(1→4) linkage and hydrolyses to glucose and galactose. Its free anomeric carbon makes it reducing, so II is false.
solution:
Lactose has a $\eta(1\to4)$ glycosidic linkage and hydrolyses to glucose and galactose. Its free anomeric carbon makes it a reducing disaccharide, so statement II is false.
Thus, statements I and III are correct.
